text:
maria.dev: Quick question — we need to codify flag precedence for the rollout docs. Example: org: featureX=false, project 'payments' sets featureX=true, route '/checkout' sets featureX=false, model 'realtime-v1' sets featureX=true. Which value should win at runtime?

aj: Short answer: most specific wins (model > route > project > org). So in your example model wins = true. :+1:

kevin_s: Is that ALWAYS? what about canary audiences where a route-level canary targets 10% of users? If route=false but model=true and the request matches the 10% canary, do we evaluate canary after scope precedence or before?

sophia-ml: Good nuance. We treat canary as an additional predicate on top of the resolved flag value. Flow: 1) determine base value by precedence (most specific scope matched) 2) evaluate rollout rules (canary buckets, user ids) that may override base only if the flag has rollout rules defined at that scope.

maria.dev: So rollouts are scoped too? If the route scope has a canary, it only applies when route is the active scope?

sophia-ml: Exactly. A canary defined at route scope applies when route is the resolved scope. If model scope exists and is more specific, model's rollout rules (if any) take precedence. We *don't* merge canaries across scopes by default.

aj: Implementation note: when a request matches multiple scopes (e.g., project + route + model), we pick the most specific scope and then evaluate that scope's value + rollout rules. If the most specific scope has no rollout rules, _no_ fallback to parent rollouts.

kevin_s: What about "deny" style flags? e.g., org=false, project=true, but route explicitly sets "force_off":true. Is "force_off" a different kind of signal?

sophia-ml: We added a guardrail: any explicit "force_off" or safety override at any scope is absolute and wins over more specific enables. So safety overrides are strongest (safety > specific scopes). We documented two tiers: safety overrides (explicit killswitchs) and normal scoped values (most specific wins).

aj: TL;DR precedence order we should document: safety_override (any scope) -> explicit scoped value (most specific wins) -> canned default from org if nothing else. Rollouts are evaluated only within the chosen scoped config.

maria.dev: That helps. Can someone drop a small config example for the doc?

taylor: Paste below, simple YAML example that we use in the runtime tests:

```
org:
  featureX: false
  safety_overrides:
    featureX: false  # global killswitch
projects:
  payments:
    featureX: true
    routes:
      /checkout:
        featureX: false
        rollout:
          bucket: user_id
          percent: 10
    models:
      realtime-v1:
        featureX: true
        rollout: null
```

aj: With that, a request hitting /checkout for a user in the 10% bucket: resolved scope = route (/checkout), route has rollout => it can flip to true for that 10%. If user not in bucket => false. If request hits model-bound endpoint and model defines true and no rollout => always true.

kevin_s: Nice. Can deploy-bot run lint to ensure nobody adds cross-scope merging rules by accident?

deploy-bot: config-lint: OK — rule-check passed for file flags/payments.yaml (no cross-scope merging detected). :white_check_mark:

maria.dev: Action items: (1) I'll update the Rollout + Flags doc with the precedence table and example YAML (2) @aj will add a unit test asserting route rollout doesn't inherit project rollouts (3) @taylor will add the safety_override note.

taylor: Got it, I'll add the safety_override section and a short example.

aj: I'll add the unit test today and link the PR here.

maria.dev: Thanks everyone — this will prevent another "why did route flip?" incident. :sweat_smile:
